title: Existing Structures, Surveys and Uncertainty
whyItMatters: Existing buildings frequently differ from historic drawings, have hidden alterations, and use older materials (wrought iron, cast iron, mild steel, unreinforced masonry). Safe refurbishment and temporary works design depend on systematic investigation and conservative engineering judgement.
introduction: Record drawings vs site reality, visual and intrusive structural appraisals, material identification and deterioration, crack diagnosis, temporary stability during alterations, and refusing to guess when opening-up is required.
objectives: Plan and interpret visual structural surveys and targeted intrusive opening-up investigations.
Identify historic materials (cast iron vs wrought iron vs steel, historic timber, lime vs cement mortar) and diagnose deterioration mechanisms.
Distinguish structural movement cracks (foundation subsidence, lintel failure, lateral wall bulge, corrosion jacking) from minor thermal/shrinkage crazing.
Design safe temporary support sequences for knock-throughs and alterations, and know when to refuse to guess and specify opening-up or specialist investigation.
learningGate: Produce a structural appraisal checklist and state what you would refuse to assume without opening up.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate percentage loss of tensile area due to reinforcement corrosion.
questions.prompt: A corroded H20 reinforcing bar (original nominal diameter 20.0 mm, original area 314.2 mm^2) is cleaned of rust during an intrusive survey and found to have a remaining minimum effective diameter of 17.0 mm (remaining area = pi * 17^2 / 4 = 227.0 mm^2). questions.explanation: Loss = (314.2 - 227.0) / 314.2 = 87.2 / 314.2 = 27.75% (note how a seemingly modest 1.5 mm radius loss removes nearly 28% of the bar’s strength!).

questions.learningObjective: Calculate axial load in temporary Acrow props supporting a needle beam during a wall knock-through.
